text: Python uses indentation to define blocks and has a large standard library.
Python web applications commonly use frameworks such as FastAPI and Django.
Python is widely used for data analysis because of libraries for arrays, tables, and visualization.
Supervised machine learning learns from labeled examples such as input-output pairs.
Unsupervised learning finds structure in data without explicit target labels.
Embedding models transform text into vectors that can be compared for semantic similarity.
RAG retrieves relevant documents and gives them to a language model as context.
A citation-aware RAG system stores source metadata alongside each chunk.
Query rewriting generates alternate formulations to improve retrieval coverage.
Reranking scores an initial candidate set with a more precise relevance model.
Fixed-size chunking creates predictable chunk lengths but can split sentences.
Sentence-aware chunking tries to preserve complete sentences inside chunks.
Paragraph-aware chunking keeps related prose together but may produce uneven sizes.
Vector databases store numerical representations and support nearest-neighbor search.
Chroma can store documents, embeddings, identifiers, and metadata for similarity search.
BM25 is a lexical ranking method that scores documents according to term relevance.
Hybrid retrieval combines lexical and semantic retrieval signals.
FastAPI provides typed HTTP endpoints and automatic OpenAPI documentation.
Streamlit can build a simple interactive interface around a Python application.
RAG evaluation should test retrieval relevance and answer correctness on a fixed dataset.
A deployed RAG service needs configuration, logging, retries, health checks, and secret management.
API keys should be stored in environment variables or a secret manager rather than source files.
Latency, retrieval scores, token usage, and errors are useful signals for debugging RAG systems.
Metadata such as source, page, section, and chunk index makes retrieval results traceable.
